chunks: May Allah deal with you! Is there no religion which unites you, nor a sense of shamefulness that sharpens you?

Is it not strange that Mu'awiya calls out to some rude, low people and they follow him without any support or grant, but when I call you, although you are the successors of Islam and the (worthy) survivors of the people, with support and distributed grants, you scatter away from me and oppose me?
Truly, there is nothing between me and you which I like and you also like it, or with which I am angry and you may also unite against it. What I love most is death!

I have taught you the Book, clarified to you arguments, apprised you of what you were ignorant and made you swallow what you were spitting out. Even a blind man would have been able to see, and he who was sleeping would have been awakened!
How ignorant of Allah is their leader Mu'awiya and their instructor Ibn an-Nabighah!
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali complain about his companions following Mu'awiya despite his own generosity?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the political pragmatism of Mu'awiya—who secured loyalty through material patronage (al-wafa') with his 'Jufat' (rough, unrefined tribesmen)—against his own spiritual authority, which he argues is superior yet less appreciated by the 'inheritance of Islam.' This reflects the broader Shia scholarly view of the early political struggle as a conflict between worldly power (muluk) and divine legitimacy (imamah), where Ali's patience is tested by the fickleness of his followers who prioritize immediate gain over enduring truth.
